documents.title: Statement of Values, Ethics and Principles for Artificial Intelligence at UNM (draft)
documents.summary: A draft statement of values, ethics and principles from UNM's AI Steering Committee (July 2026). It sets high-level principles on human agency, trust and sustainability and tells community members to follow course expectations. It sets no rule on student AI use.
documents.stance_why: The statement lists principles such as 'AI should augment rather than replace human judgment' and asks members to understand 'when AI use is permitted or limited' and follow 'course expectations'. It bans or allows nothing itself, leaving the specific rules to courses and other policies, so delegates.

units.anchor: AI should augment rather than replace human judgment, expertise, responsibility, and relationships.
units.fit_note: Applies to all UNM community members and to human relationships and expertise, not just the student as problem-solver.

notes: Coder B. Only included documents coded (5). Computing, school and course layers not found/deferred per the collect file. The syllabus-language page reproduces sample statements from other institutions (OSU, Temple, UT Tyler, DePaul, Brockport, Ontario Tech); I coded them as policies UNM publishes as models, with the sample text attributed to UNM's page. Several student-use sentences repeat across the provost memo options and addendum; I coded the distinct statements and skipped exact repeats.
